textos.Celebración campesina de la trilla del t: A peasant celebration of the wheat and maize threshing, with one-pot food, coplas and drum music. A good excuse to discover the rural side of the town on the Tropic of Capricorn.

textos.Ciudad histórica de calles empedradas, d: Historic city of cobbled streets, declared a World Heritage Site with the entire Quebrada. It is the gateway to the deep north and the starting point to Hornocal.
textos.Colectivos urbanos e interurbanos entre: Urban and intercity buses between San Salvador, Palpalá, Perico and El Carmen, running all day. Gobernador Horacio Guzmán airport is in Perico, 33 km from the capital. The dams and Termas de Reyes are reached on a half-day tour, by local taxi or in your own car.

textos.Con dos días más: sumá el tren solar y l: With two more days: add the solar train and the Puna from Tres Cruces to La Quiaca and Yavi (see extended itinerary).
textos.Con un día más, seguí la RP83 hasta San: With one more day, continue along the RP83 to San Francisco and Santa Bárbara, or go up to the Quebrada the next day (130 km on the RN9).
textos.Corsos, murgas y comparsas barriales, co: Parades, murgas and neighborhood troupes, with water and foam in the streets. The Carnival of the Valleys is urban and nocturnal: there is dancing until dawn in the clubs and on the street.
textos.Cosecha de los viñedos de altura con deg: Harvest from the high altitude vineyards with tastings, live music and the election of the queen. The Quebrada wine is made between 2,300 and 2,800 meters.
textos.Cuesta del Lipán: la subida a 4.170 m, c: Cuesta del Lipán: the climb to 4,170 m, with viewpoints over the ravine

textos.De Purmamarca a Humahuaca pueblo por pue: From Purmamarca to Humahuaca town by town, with Salinas Grandes and the Cerro de los 14 Colores. Adding two days you enter the Puna seriously.
textos.De abril a noviembre, cielos limpios y f: From April to November, clear skies and dry cold. From January to March, short rains that complicate dirt roads.
textos.De altura: vinos orgánicos de Jujuy: De altura: vinos orgánicos de Jujuy
textos.De mayo a octubre, con menos lluvia, est: From May to October, with less rain, the jungle trails are open and the cliff-side road holds up. A good time for birdwatching: birds come out early and the fog lifts before noon.
textos.De mayo a octubre, con menos lluvia. En: From May to October, with less rain. In summer the dirt roads are closed and the heat is intense.
textos.De noche y con viento, manejá con precau: At night and in wind, drive carefully: there are loose animals and fog banks on the climb.
textos.De sur a norte: cada punto con su kilóme: South to north: each stop with its distance from San Salvador de Jujuy and its altitude. Scroll along the line.
textos.Decenas de bandas de sikuris y aerófonos: Dozens of Andean sikuris and aerophone bands from all over Puna are found in the historic city. A weekend of drums, panpipes and parades through the cobbled streets.
textos.Degustaciones en bodegas boutique (Tilca: Tastings at boutique wineries (Tilcara and Maimará)
textos.Del altiplano a la selva hay casi 4.000: From the high plateau to the jungle there are almost 4,000 metres of elevation gain and four different trips inside the same province. These are the regions on the map —the same four as the logo— with their towns, the transport you can take and the tourist information offices in each one.
textos.Directorio orientativo: los locales, los: Guidance directory: venues, band names and live music days change season by season. Ask at the inn or tourist office on the same day — and book in January, Carnival, Easter and August.
textos.Dormir la primera noche a 2.300 m (y no: Sleeping the first night at 2,300 m (and not in Humahuaca) is the best way to acclimatise before going up to the Salinas.

textos.Dónde se come y se escucha folklore desp: Where you eat and listen to folklore after the sun goes down, from the Quebrada to the capital. Dinner from 9 p.m., live folklore from 10:30 p.m. and main show around midnight.
textos.Efectivo en pesos suficiente para 3 o 4: Cash in pesos enough for 3 or 4 days
textos.El Centro de Visitantes Aguas Negras, de: The Aguas Negras Visitor Center, inside the park on RP83, is open every day from 8 a.m. to 7 p.m. and collects reports. The National Park Administration is in the town of Calilegua (Marinero A. López s/n, 03886 578465).
textos.El Cerro de los Siete Colores sobre el p: El Cerro de los Siete Colores sobre el pueblo de Purmamarca
textos.El Pucará de Tilcara con su monumento de: El Pucará de Tilcara con su monumento de piedra y cardones
textos.El Vía Crucis sube por las laderas con c: The Via Crucis climbs the slopes with hundreds of faithful, and the nightly processions illuminate the stone streets. Everything fills up: reserve accommodation months in advance.
textos.El altiplano ocupa todo el oeste de la p: The high plateau occupies the entire west of the province: a plateau of salt flats, meadows and mountain ranges where the horizon is wider than the towns. The air is so dry that the sky looks darker, and the night falls below freezing almost all year round, even in January.
textos.El borde del salar, donde el horizonte s: The edge of the salt flat, where the horizon becomes a white line
textos.El camino al Hornocal es de montaña sin: The road to Hornocal is a mountain track without guard rails. Do not go up in the rain or in a low car; ask about the state of the road at the Humahuaca tourist office.
textos.El campanario de la iglesia de Uquía con: El campanario de la iglesia de Uquía contra el cielo
textos.El carnaval andino: desentierro del diab: Andean carnival: the unearthing of the devil (or the mojón) in every town, comparsas, flour, talcum powder and coplas to the sound of the erkencho and the drum. In Tilcara and Maimará the unearthing starts on Saturday; on Ash Wednesday the chaya is danced and the burial of the carnival closes the following Sunday.
textos.El feriado trasladable se confirma por d: The transferable holiday is confirmed by decree
textos.El mes de la Madre Tierra: se abre la bo: The month of Mother Earth: the mouth of the earth is opened, food, chicha and coca leaves are offered. August 1st are the central events, but throughout the month there are ceremonies, fairs and music in the towns.
textos.El mirador de la Cuesta del Lipán es el: The Cuesta del Lipán viewpoint is the highest point of the trip: do not exert yourself there. If you are travelling with children, check how they feel before going on.
textos.El otro Jujuy, el que baja en lugar de s: The other Jujuy, the one that goes down instead of up: mountain jungle, clear rivers and the city where the trip is put together. No altitude, no soroche.
textos.El pueblo más fotografiado del norte juj: The most photographed town in the north of Jujuy, nestled at the mouth of the Quebrada. It is covered in an afternoon, but the light of dawn and dusk is another trip.
textos.El pueblo más pequeño de la Quebrada y e: The smallest town in the Quebrada and the most famous for its colonial art: the church houses the series of Ángeles Arquebuceros, a mestizo painting from the 17th century.
textos.El pueblo que es Patrimonio de la Humani: El pueblo que es Patrimonio de la Humanidad y corazón de la Quebrada de Humahuaca | Tilcara, Jujuy
textos.El pueblo y el parque nacional que le da: The town and the national park that gives it its name, at the foot of the mountain range: the gateway to the mountain jungle and kilometer zero of the RP83, which climbs towards the Puna to the east.
textos.El salar de Salinas Grandes con sus pile: El salar de Salinas Grandes con sus piletones y montañas de sal
textos.El solsticio de invierno y el año nuevo: The winter solstice and the new year of the Andean peoples. Ceremonies at dawn with offerings to Pachamama, sikuris music and fire. In Tilcara it is made in Pucará; in Humahuaca, at the viewpoints at dawn.
textos.El tren tiene pocas frecuencias y lugare: The train has few departures and limited seats: book online before planning the rest of the itinerary.
textos.Elegí origen y destino sobre la RN9, los: I chose origin and destination on the RN9, the branches to Salinas Grandes, Hornocal and Yavi, or the descent to Calilegua and Valle Grande.
textos.En la Quebrada y la Puna vas a dormir en: In the Quebrada and the Puna you will sleep between 2,300 and 3,400 m. Altitude sickness (soroche) comes from climbing too fast, not from being unfit. In the Valles and the foothills of the Yungas, below 2,000 m, altitude is not an issue.
textos.En la RP83 no hay estaciones de servicio: There are no petrol stations on the RP83 and the phone signal drops for much of the road.
textos.En la selva se camina con manga larga y: In the jungle you walk in long sleeves and with repellent, even when it is hot: there are mosquitoes and ticks.
textos.Entre pueblos la señal de celular se cor: Between towns the mobile signal drops and many places have no internet or card reader.

textos.Jujuy tiene cuatro regiones —Puna, Quebr: Jujuy has four regions —Puna, Quebrada, Valles and Yungas— and almost every trip starts in the two northern ones. Here is the full map: distances between towns, altitude above sea level, which festival is taking shape this week and where to hear live music tonight — no surprises from altitude, fuel or phone signal.

textos.La Quebrada como puerta de entrada al al: The Quebrada as a gateway to the high plateau: valleys, Puna Jujeña, the border with Bolivia and the towns on the slope.
textos.La Quebrada pueblo por pueblo, en el ord: La Quebrada town by town, in the order of the route, and an entry point for each of the other three regions: the Puna salt flat, the Yungas jungle and the capital of the Valleys.
textos.La RP83 es de cornisa y angosta: manejá: The RP83 is a narrow cliff-side road: drive by day, slowly, and watch out for wildlife and cyclists.
textos.La capital cultural de la Quebrada: cent: The cultural capital of the Quebrada: a centre for archaeological research, peñas every night and one of the most important pre-Hispanic sites in north-west Argentina.
textos.La capital provincial, entre los ríos Gr: The provincial capital, between the Grande and Xibi Xibi rivers, with the airport and the terminal from which almost the entire trip departs. It has a cathedral, town hall and a market worth an entire morning.
textos.La capital tiene el circuito de peñas má: The capital has the most constant peña circuit in the province, all year round: dinner, guitar and folklore from Tuesday to Saturday. It is also where you can hear bands from the Puna and the Yungas on the same weekend.
textos.La catedral de San Salvador de Jujuy fre: La catedral de San Salvador de Jujuy frente a la plaza
textos.La ciudad más grande y la más tradiciona: The largest and most traditional city. Multi-storey peñas, sikuri groups that appear after the procession and copleros singing to the drum in the open street.
textos.La dosis mínima de Quebrada, bien armada: The minimum dose of Quebrada, well prepared: a single change of accommodation, the three must-sees and a climb to 3,400 m to test the altitude.
textos.La fiesta grande de la Puna y de la fron: The big festival of the Puna and the border with Bolivia: procession, dances, bands and fair. If you travel to the deep north in December, it is the date to see.
textos.La fiesta más grande de los Valles: carr: The biggest festival in the Valleys: floats, parades and stands set up by the schools throughout the second fortnight. It is the week when the capital is filled with students from all over the province.
textos.La franja baja y húmeda del sureste, con: The low, humid strip of the southeast, with cane fields, citrus trees and tobacco over a wide valley. Most of the provincial population lives here and there is San Salvador, the capital, with the airport through which almost all tourism enters.
textos.La información de esta guía es de refere: The information in this guide is for reference and may change: transportation schedules, road openings and festival dates are updated season by season.
textos.La mayor concentración de peñas de la Qu: The biggest concentration of peñas in the Quebrada: locro or llama dinner, guitar, bombo drum and copleros. At weekends there are live bands and sometimes dancing until 3 a.m.
textos.La música en vivo aparece en las fiestas: Live music appears at festivities and fairs, not on a night circuit. In La Quiaca, on weekends there is dancing with local bands.
textos.La selva de montaña cambia de piso con c: The mountain jungle changes floor with each curve: foothills, montane and cloud forest in less than 25 km. You walk in the morning and with a local guide, when the birds are active.
textos.La selva de montaña que trepa por el est: The mountain jungle that climbs to the east: clouds hanging on the hills, giant ferns and humidity that is unlike anything in the rest of Jujuy. It is the southern end of the Andean yungas, a green corridor that continues to Bolivia.

textos.Las familias velan a sus muertos toda la: Families keep vigil for their dead all night with food, music and flowers. The offerings and candles in the cemetery on the Painter's Palette are one of the strongest images of the year.
textos.Las fechas de carnaval, Semana Santa y a: The dates of carnival, Easter and some patron saint festivals are mobile. Always confirm with the municipality's tourist office or the festival commission: the schedules of the parades and the sikuris bands are set up on the fly.

Purmamarca is 3 km off the RN9 and only served by local buses, every 2 hours. The Solar Train runs on the old Belgrano track: 42 km and six stations (Volcán, Tumbaya, Purmamarca, Posta de Hornillos, Maimará and Tilcara), with a ticket office at Belgrano 493 in the capital. Every town has local taxis and minibuses.

textos.Micros desde la terminal de San Salvador: Buses from the San Salvador terminal to Abra Pampa, Tres Cruces and La Quiaca (El Quiaqueño, Panamericano, Jama), and to Susques on the RN52. textos.lluvias de tarde, caminos de tierra comp: afternoon rain, difficult dirt roads and routes to the Puna that may be closed. Winter (May to September) is dry, with nights below freezing.
textos.mangas largas, repelente y calzado cerra: long sleeves, repellent and closed shoes. The trails are made in the morning; after summer rains they may close.
textos.mercado central, peñas urbanas y la Fies: the central market, urban peñas and the National Students' Festival in September.
textos.nada de trekking exigente ni alcohol la: no strenuous trekking and no alcohol on the first night.
for gravel, loose stone and mud.
textos.para tramos cortos entre pueblo y pueblo: for short hops between villages, especially at night.
textos.pomelos y naranjas en El Carmen, tabaco: grapefruits and oranges in El Carmen, tobacco in Perico and Monterrico.
textos.práctica para Salinas Grandes y Hornocal: handy for Salinas Grandes and Hornocal, where the access is gravel and needs a high-clearance vehicle.
textos.recorrido turístico sobre la vieja vía d: a tourist ride along the old Belgrano railway line, with stops at the Quebrada stations. Book ahead: departures are limited.
textos.remera, abrigo polar y campera cortavien: T-shirt, fleece and a waterproof windproof jacket. You will use all of them on the same day.
textos.retablos dorados y pintura mestiza de lo: gilded altarpieces and mestizo painting from the 17th and 18th centuries in the towns along the route.
textos.salen desde la terminal de San Salvador: they leave from the San Salvador de Jujuy bus terminal and stop in every town; good frequency as far as Humahuaca, much less towards the Puna.
textos.salí antes de las 9 h, la mejor luz es d: leave before 9 a.m., the best light is in the morning. It is a mountain gravel road: high-clearance vehicle or a booked tour, never a low car.
textos.se compran en cualquier feria; el mate d: they are sold at any market; coca tea helps with headaches.
you go in with a high-clearance vehicle or a tour. After rain the salt crust softens and some sections become impassable.
textos.terrazas de cultivo de origen prehispáni: cultivation terraces of pre-Hispanic origin that are still in use for corn, potatoes and quinoa.
textos.trapiches y cultivos de las colonias del: sugar mills and crops in the colonies of Valle Grande and Santa Bárbara.
textos.vicuñas, llamas y suris, el avestruz and: vicuñas, llamas and suris, the Andean ostrich that runs along the slopes.
textos.y avisá a alguien tu recorrido antes de: and tell someone your route before heading out to the Puna.
textos.y temprano; las cenas pesadas empeoran e: and early; heavy dinners make you feel worse.
textos.yaguareté, tapir, pavas de monte y urrac: jaguar, tapir, wild turkeys and magpies; about 350 species of birds.
